Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 106, verses 1–2:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called Quraysh, because it mentions the tribe of Quraysh and touches upon some aspects of their circumstances.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• To remind the people of Makkah of Allah's blessing upon them in their provision and in their being made secure from fears, and to couple this reminder with the command to single out Allah in worship, because of the blessings He has lavished upon them and the calamities He has averted from them.

[Tafsir]

Marvel at the familiarity of Quraysh (ilaf Quraysh), their security, the soundness of their affairs, and the regularity of their two journeys: in winter to Yemen and in summer to Syria (al-Sham), and the facilitation of that to bring them what they need.

• To remind the people of Makkah of Allah's blessing upon them in their provision and in their being made secure from fears, and to couple this reminder with the command to single out Allah in worship, because of the blessings He has lavished upon them and the calamities He has averted from them.

[Tafsir]

Marvel at the familiarity of Quraysh (ilaf Quraysh), their security, the soundness of their affairs, and the regularity of their two journeys: in winter to Yemen and in summer to Syria (al-Sham), and the facilitation of that to bring them what they need.

So let them worship the Lord of this House, the Ka'bah, the House they take pride in, and through which they have gained honor and eminence. Let them give thanks and single Him out, sincerely devoting their worship to Him alone.
Who fed them against severe hunger, and made them safe from great terror and fear.
